headline: Bug in FIFA World Cup internal system gave anyone ability to modify TV stream
summary: A security flaw allowed a researcher to access internal FIFA platforms, giving full control over the World Cup TV stream and commentator screens globally.
details: A security researcher, known as BobDaHacker, discovered a critical flaw in FIFA's internal systems. This vulnerability granted her full control over the TV stream for every World Cup game, including what was displayed on screens for broadcasters and commentators worldwide.

The researcher gained access by simply registering as a player agent on FIFA's official platform. A subsequent flaw in FIFA's back-end API failed to verify proper user authorization, enabling her to reach several internal platforms.

BobDaHacker highlighted the severe implications, stating that a single attacker could have simultaneously hijacked every camera. She noted that an attacker could have "rickrolled the entire FIFA World Cup" with this exploit.

The flaw was reported on Tuesday night Japan time and FIFA addressed the issue within a few hours. However, FIFA did not acknowledge the researcher's report and did not immediately respond to TechCrunch's request for comment.
